statement: Given a number x and an integer n, return x raised to the power n.
Use binary exponentiation with recursion: xⁿ = (x^(n/2))² when n is even, and x × (x^((n − 1)/2))² when n is odd, with x⁰ = 1. This needs only O(log |n|) multiplications.
When n is negative, compute x^|n| and return 1 / x^|n|.

examples.explanation: 2¹⁰ = (2⁵)² and 2⁵ = 2 × (2²)², so a few squarings give 1024.
n is negative, so 2³ = 8 is computed first and then inverted: 1 / 8 = 0.125.
An odd power keeps the sign of a negative base: (−2)⁵ = −32.

constraints: either x is not zero or n > 0
